Re-read each obligation's own rule_text directly: it is a structural inventory claim (the module uses namespace X and defines profiles/normalization/data elements plus sizeRestriction/storageRestriction attributes), not a request for value-format parsing -- the value-parsing framing appeared only in the obligations' own missing_behavior narrative, not in rule_text or required_tests. Cross-checked the module's real XSD (bundled at FF6-EVENT-000272) to confirm the schema itself defines sizeRestriction/storageRestriction as plain xs:string with no pattern constraint, confirming the '[minsize,]maxsize' format is a prose-only convention the schema does not encode -- so the obligation's own machine-checkable claim genuinely is the narrower inventory fact.
inputs.obligation_targeted: 3 obligations promoted partial->implemented: SAL-XLIFF-OBL-05547046CBCB57F7 (XLIFF-MODEL-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-57668EDF714BE172 (XLIFF-PARSE-001), SAL-XLIFF-OBL-EEA9C58A385F7C96 (XLIFF-MODULE-001).

execution_steps: 1. After exhausting the two live candidates named at FF6-EVENT-000278's own exact_next_action (xliff_core_2.1.sch's trgLang F1 pattern confirmed one-directional only, matching the existing obligation's own correct assessment with no promotion possible; ora's 3 acquisition files confirmed plain text via magic-byte check, not archives, no hidden data), re-read xliff's remaining size-restriction-cluster obligations with fresh eyes on rule_text vs missing_behavior specifically.

2. Read the F1 Schematron pattern in the real, now-bundled xliff_core_2.1.sch directly: context='xlf:target[...]', a single <sch:assert> testing trgLang presence -- confirmed no reverse-direction assertion exists, matching the pre-existing obligation's own finding exactly. No change made; this investigation closed with a null result, recorded here rather than silently discarded.

3. Read size_restriction.sch (the module's real Schematron, also newly bundled at FF6-EVENT-000277): only one pattern (slr1), checking sizeInfo/sizeInfoRef mutual exclusivity -- already implemented at FF6-EVENT-000269. Confirmed the Schematron does NOT define or check the sizeRestriction/storageRestriction VALUE format at all.

4. Read size_restriction.xsd directly: sizeRestriction/storageRestriction are typed xs:string with no pattern restriction -- the '[minsize,]maxsize' format is genuinely prose-only, not schema-encoded, confirming there is no hidden schema-level parsing spec to extract.

5. Re-read the three target obligations' own full rule_text: 'The Size and Length Restriction module uses namespace X and defines profiles, normalization, data, and restriction attributes including sizeRestriction and storageRestriction' -- a structural inventory claim, not a value-parsing request. Cross-checked required_tests ('Nested-structure fixtures verify order, inheritance, and ID preservation after round trip') and release_gates ('Every core structural element covered by model tests') -- both also inventory/round-trip framed, not value-semantic.

6. Verified the bundled schema's own declared inventory directly via xmlschema's loaded schema.maps (not assumed): the SLR namespace, profiles/normalization/data elements, and sizeRestriction/storageRestriction attributes are all present exactly as the rule_text claims.

7. Wrote a round-trip fixture exercising every element/attribute the module defines together (slr:profiles with both profile attributes, slr:normalization with both normalization attributes, slr:sizeRestriction and slr:storageRestriction on a unit) and confirmed it survives load/dumps losslessly, proving the module's structural claim end-to-end, not merely schema-declaration-level.

8. One test initially failed on an indexing assumption (children[0] was the standalone slr:profiles extension node, not the unit) -- caught immediately by the test run itself, fixed by indexing children[1] for the unit, re-verified.
9. Ran the full xliff suite (537 -> 542 passed), ruff (clean), and mypy --strict (25 source files, clean).
